the-domain-is-an-axis.statement: The corpus varies the interpretive DOMAIN the way it varies any other feature, so no reading of the marks is privileged and none can be.
the-domain-is-an-axis.scope: About whether a domain can be privileged, not about whether the acoustic one is attested. It is: Sol-Center labels its two lateral axes Frequency and Level and names its centre cells Harmony and Discord, and ZodiacSignSymbols carries a Cromatic Tone column.

the-drawn-ticks-sit-just-above-the-legib.statement: Both hand-drawn dependent marks clear the derived legibility floor, and one of them barely.
the-drawn-ticks-sit-just-above-the-legib.success_condition: A drawn dependent mark below the floor that a reader can still resolve.

the-four-floors-are-one-floor.statement: Four rules that look unrelated are the same inequality: a feature exists while it is wider than the pen.
the-four-floors-are-one-floor.derivation: Two marks resolve while the dependent one is at least w/r of the anchor. An enclosure survives while its inscribed radius exceeds w/2. Nesting continues while the ring between levels, s^k (1-s), exceeds w. A stroke's turning exists only down to a spacing of w. Each was derived separately and each reduces to the same comparison against the same quantity.
the-four-floors-are-one-floor.given: the four rules themselves, two of which are measured rather than proved: that an enclosure survives while its inscribed radius exceeds half the pen width (19 of 21), and that nesting is bounded by the gap between levels rather than by the innermost size.

the-gathers-width-is-not-a-separate-axis.statement: How BROAD a run's gather is adds nothing the grid does not already have. Widening it only makes the fit worse.
the-gathers-width-is-not-a-separate-axis.success_condition: A gather width that fits better than the narrowest.

the-generated-lexicon-contains-the-bench.statement: BOTH hand-drawn Challenge Symbols are entries the corpus generated without having seen them: the left at distance 0.072 in the two-mark lexicon, the right at 0.218 in the three-mark lexicon.
the-generated-lexicon-contains-the-bench.success_condition: A feature of the left symbol that no generated entry carries.

the-grammar-gaps-are-the-frame-bound-sch.statement: Of the four relational schemas with no attested operator, three -- UP/DOWN, FRONT/BACK and PATH -- are the frame-bound ones and constitute a single gap. PART/WHOLE is frame-free and mereological, and is a separate absence.
the-grammar-gaps-are-the-frame-bound-sch.derivation: The attested operators are frame-free and the directional schemas are not, measured as drift under global rotation: at most 3.5e-2 for the attested against 2.20 and 4.40 for UP/DOWN and FRONT/BACK. So the inventory could never have contained them.

the-kernel-halves-the-position-axis.statement: Where a run gathers its turning is readable only up to reflection about the run's middle, because reversing a run is in the kernel.
the-kernel-halves-the-position-axis.derivation: Direction of travel leaves the ink unchanged. A run that gathers at position p, travelled the other way, gathers at 1 - p and inks identically. So the axis is not position but DISTANCE FROM THE MIDDLE, |p - 0.5|, and it runs over half the range anyone would write down.
the-kernel-halves-the-position-axis.given: that direction of travel is in the kernel, which is measured -- a run and its reverse ink identically at 0.0000 against a floor of 0.026. Given that, the halving is arithmetic.

the-notation-is-flat-until-containment.statement: The notation can coordinate but cannot subordinate. Recursion requires containment, and containment is not expressible in it.
the-notation-is-flat-until-containment.derivation: Embedding a constituent inside a constituent requires 'inside' to be readable. Containment cannot be read from the placement parameters, measured: on a lobed closed figure a Point at separation 0.75 is inside along a lobe and outside in a notch, with identical r, bearing and scale. A circle is the one shape for which separation decides containment, which is why testing the question on a circle passes falsely.
the-notation-is-flat-until-containment.success_condition: A derivation of separation-cannot-decide-containment that does not depend on measuring these particular figures would carry this up with it.

the-notation-is-readable-except-at-small.statement: Of 191 depth-2 constructions, 145 share a figure with another -- but only 5 of those collisions are non-trivial, and every non-degenerate one is caused by a nested mark being too small to show its curvature class.
the-notation-is-readable-except-at-small.success_condition: The relative scale below which curvature class stops being recoverable, measured rather than assumed. That number is the notation's legibility floor and `nest`'s 0.4 should be set from it.
the-notation-is-readable-except-at-small.scope: Depth 2 only. Depth 3 is not enumerated and may collide differently.

the-one-run-lexicon.statement: The tables generate a lexicon rather than only describing one. Forty one-run entries survive reachability and the pipeline's own read-back error, each with a reading derived from its geometry, and all four marks that live on these axes fall inside it.
the-one-run-lexicon.success_condition: A mark the corpus names that this grid cannot reach, or two entries a reader could not tell apart.

the-orbit-count-is-tolerance-bounded.statement: The orbit count is not an exact integer the corpus can assert. Across the interval its own calibration calls safe it runs 89 to 94, and doubling the rotation search does not settle it. 93 is the central value, not a constant.
the-orbit-count-is-tolerance-bounded.scope: About the count, not about the partition's structure. The 191 constructions are themselves exact and symmetric: 5 binary operators x 36 ordered pairs, plus reflect_pair on all 6 marks, plus close on 5 -- a Point has nothing to close. Nothing here disturbs any claim about which figures are related; it bounds only how many distinct ones there are.

the-pair-is-the-unit-of-assignment.statement: Meaning is assigned to mark PAIRS, not to marks. A domain that names one mark of a pair names its partner, without exception, and the grid is sparse enough that this is not true by construction.
the-pair-is-the-unit-of-assignment.scope: MEASURED over this census, whose entries are individually cited but which I assembled. The construction risk is that I recorded a word only when I could find its partner. Three things argue against it and none of them closes it: F134's table shows the sparse-but-paired shape before the census existed; the one unbalanced cell (temporal Point/Circle, 3 against 2) survives unpadded; and the contested pair (Amperage/Voltage) is recorded as contested rather than resolved to fit. The falsifier is a domain word on one mark whose partner has none, found by re-reading the sheets.

the-pen-to-ink-map-has-a-kernel.statement: Six things the hand can vary leave the ink unchanged, and therefore can never carry meaning in this notation, however natural they are to a writer.
the-pen-to-ink-map-has-a-kernel.derivation: The writing system is a map from what the hand does to what survives on the page, and it is not injective. The things it collapses are exactly the things unavailable to the notation. This generalises the grammar rule `no-reading-order-in-ink`, which named one member of the kernel; there are at least six, and stroke order is not the most consequential. Retracing is: a run may be gone over any number of times and the ink is the same, so the notation has no way to say `again`.
the-pen-to-ink-map-has-a-kernel.success_condition: A pen variation that is in the kernel and that the corpus nonetheless uses to distinguish two symbols. There would then be two symbols with identical ink.

the-pen-width-is-the-notations-unit.statement: Absolute scale is not open after all. The pen width is an intrinsic unit: it can be read off any drawing without asking its author anything, and every length in the notation can be stated in it.
the-pen-width-is-the-notations-unit.derivation: Table G.3 was open on the grounds that nothing fixes a unit, so a figure and the same figure twice as large say the same thing. But the second figure is drawn with a pen twice as wide or it is not the same figure -- and if the pen is NOT scaled, the two figures differ in every one of the four floors, which is a difference the page carries. The unit is therefore in the drawing already.
the-pen-width-is-the-notations-unit.given: that a drawing is made with a pen of some width -- which is true of every drawing there is, but is a fact about drawing rather than about the notation.

the-pipelines-own-floor-is-0.05.statement: Nothing this corpus draws can score below about 0.05 against an extracted figure, because the extraction does not return what it was given.
the-pipelines-own-floor-is-0.05.success_condition: A generated figure that round-trips closer than the perturbation spread.

the-roster-confused-unmeasured-with-unme.statement: Every dimension the complexifier roster marked BLIND is cheaply measurable. Not one was a limit of the geometry; all were limits of the code that had been written.
the-roster-confused-unmeasured-with-unme.success_condition: A dimension along which ink varies that genuinely cannot be measured.

the-transformations-panel-is-the-element.statement: The cheat sheet's transformations 3x3 draws four inverse pairs around a centre, and the pair that looked like a fourth mark pair is not one: In/Out are the BARRED triangles and Rise/Fall the UNBARRED ones, so the panel reads the direction opposition at both settings of the crossbar bit.
the-transformations-panel-is-the-element.scope: One panel on one sheet, measured. Says nothing about the other 31 cells of the opposition census, which were read independently.

thesaurus-size-depends-on-mirroring.statement: The depth-2 sign inventory is 93 if mirroring carries no meaning and 103 if it does.
thesaurus-size-depends-on-mirroring.derivation: Re-running the enumeration quotienting by rotation alone rather than by rotation and reflection gives 103 orbits against 93. Only 10 of the 93 split, because for the other 30 chiral orbits these operators never construct the enantiomorph -- it is permitted by the geometry and unreachable at this depth.
thesaurus-size-depends-on-mirroring.scope: Depth 2, after the F105 correction to concatenate. Before that fix the pair read 80/88; the operator was placing its marks apart rather than joining them, which collapsed concatenate into superpose_displaced across most of the space. THE 93 IS TOLERANCE-BOUNDED: see the-orbit-count-is-tolerance-bounded, which measures it at 89 to 94 across the interval the calibration licenses. Cite it as a central value, not an exact count.

theta0-is-60.statement: Aries begins 60 degrees clockwise from the top on every wheel in the corpus.
theta0-is-60.success_condition: A reason for 60 rather than 0 or 90. Remarkable as stability across five years; says nothing about necessity.

thinning-splits-a-crossing-into-two-tees.statement: A skeleton cannot hold four strands meeting at one pixel and stay one pixel wide, so every X in a photographed figure arrives as two Y junctions joined by a stub.
thinning-splits-a-crossing-into-two-tees.success_condition: A photographed crossing that thins to a single point of valence 4 without merging.

three-cells-restate-the-geometry.statement: Three of the thirty-two attested domain-pair cells name the curvature itself, so they cannot be evidence for any semantic polarity aligned with curvature. Counting all thirty-two counts the premise three times.
three-cells-restate-the-geometry.scope: A fact about which cells can bear weight, not about whether the polarity is real.

three-marks-bracket-by-connectivity-not-.statement: A three-mark symbol is not a flat product of three cells. Its bracketing is fixed by which relation joins the ink.
three-marks-bracket-by-connectivity-not-.derivation: The grammar's first rule is that constituency is connectivity. A relation that joins the ink -- crossing, abutting, overlapping, containing -- leaves ONE constituent, which can anchor a third mark. A relation that does not -- apart -- leaves two, and a third mark placed against them has no single thing to be placed against. So the only bracketing available is (connected pair) plus a mark apart.
three-marks-bracket-by-connectivity-not-.given: `connectivity-is-constituency`, which is measured rather than proved.

three-wave-families.statement: There are three wave families, and a figure can belong to one by CHARACTER while a different figure generates it by TILING. Generatively: Angle repeated is the triangle wave, Staple alternating is the square wave, Wave repeated is the sine wave. Characterologically: Angle is the triangle family, Line and Staple the square family, Curve and Wave the sine family. Closing the same generator gives that family's polygon: Angle at apex 60 degrees closes to an equilateral triangle and the Staple with body equal to upright closes to a square. The sine family is the exception -- the Wave closes to a lens and the Circle is already closed.
three-wave-families.derivation: GENERATIVE: tile each mark along its own axis and compare the run to the defined wave as a FUNCTION -- y over a shared grid at unit amplitude, over one detected period, phase and polarity free, by trimmed RMS. Angle 0.002, Staple 0.005, Wave 0.002. Floor 0.02 (the largest disagreement between an ideal wave and the same wave at another frequency over two to six periods); nearest two ideals 0.147 apart, seven times that. The Curve's tiling is 0.272 from the nearest ideal; the Line's and the Circle's profiles are flat, so they have no period. CHARACTEROLOGICAL: curvature class separates the smooth family, and the direction of the straight runs separates the other two. A figure whose every run is axis-parallel or axis-perpendicular keeps its angles under any axis-aligned stretch; one with runs at any other angle does not. Angle runs at 45 and 135; Line at 0; Staple and the square wave at 0 and 90. POLYGON: close the generator -- join its free ends with a chord -- and compare to the regular polygon under rotation and reflection. Equilateral triangle 0.045, square 0.0035, against a same-figure tolerance of 0.073. Each needs its free proportion set: a chevron closes to an isoceles triangle at any apex and an equilateral one only at sixty degrees.
three-wave-families.scope: About the alphabet, not about the twelve. Establishes which figure generates which wave and which belongs to which family, and says nothing about what a wave form MEANS. The Staple is not one of the six marks -- it is Line with a perpendicular upright at each end.

topology-depends-on-how-thickly-you-writ.statement: A figure's readable topology is not a property of the figure alone. The same curve written with a thicker pen encloses fewer regions, and the threshold is exact enough to predict.
topology-depends-on-how-thickly-you-writ.success_condition: A figure whose inked topology differs from the rule's prediction by more than the raster can resolve.

turning-is-read-back-to-a-floor-plus-a-p.statement: Turning read back off ink is accurate to about 30 degrees plus 9 per cent of itself, while the figure stays clear of itself -- and collapses entirely when it does not.
turning-is-read-back-to-a-floor-plus-a-p.success_condition: A well-cleared figure whose turning reads back outside this band, or a figure below 1.5 pen widths of clearance whose turning survives.

two-marks-stand-in-exactly-six-ways.statement: There are six ways two marks can stand to each other, and the six are forced rather than chosen: fused, contained, overlapping, crossing, abutting, apart.
two-marks-stand-in-exactly-six-ways.derivation: Two yes-or-no questions exhaust the cases. Do they share a point? Is one inside a bounded region of the other? That gives four cells; the sharing cell splits by whether a stroke ENDS at the meeting, which is the same parity that separates a T from an X; and one further cell exists because some pairs are not two marks at all. Marks laid exactly on each other, and marks butted end to end, both make ink that a single unbroken run would make, so the page holds ONE mark. FUSED is that cell.
two-marks-stand-in-exactly-six-ways.given: the same model of ink the retracing claim rests on -- that ink is a SET of covered points. Five of the six cells follow from the two questions alone; FUSED needs the model, because it says a second pass over the same place adds nothing.

two-unnamed-orbits-sit-beside-named-ones.statement: Of the four figures the corpus draws, two have an unnamed orbit within 0.085 of them and two have nothing within 0.35. The infinity sign, attested as reflect_pair(Wave), sits 0.081 from superpose_displaced(Circle,Circle) -- two circles set side by side.
two-unnamed-orbits-sit-beside-named-ones.scope: A fact about these 93 representatives under this metric. It says nothing about meaning, and the two isolated cases -- Sun-in-Circle and the cross -- are equally a result: they have no near neighbour at all.

ul-is-not-phonetic.statement: Universal Symbology is not a phonetic system, so comparing its marks to the letters of a phonetic alphabet is a category comparison, not a measurement -- regardless of how well it is instrumented.
ul-is-not-phonetic.derivation: The six marks are individuated by symmetry order and curvature class (F84/F85/F88), which are geometric properties. A phonetic letter is individuated by the sound it records. Nothing maps one onto the other, and the corpus's own `Instruction Manual - Universal Symbology - Vocalization and Language` states vocalization as a GOAL rather than a result (F31), so the bridge that would license the comparison does not exist.

up-is-shared-across-canvases.statement: WITHDRAWN. Asked whether two readers on different canvases assign the same direction to `up`.
up-is-shared-across-canvases.why_withdrawn: They do not, and this corpus had already derived why. `orientation-is-a-canvas-parameter` (derived, F103) says the frame always supplies an orientation and never canonically, and its own derivation carries the counterexample: inside a cosmic supervoid the pull is outward from every side, so `down` inverts. The question had an answer on file the whole time, and the answer is no. What was actually at stake was whether any MEANING in the notation depends on the agreement, and it does not -- see `direction-is-read-as-contrast`.

updown-is-meaningful.statement: Up and down are distinguishable on the page and carry meaning -- given a canvas, which always supplies them and never canonically.
updown-is-meaningful.success_condition: This is an embedding assumption, not a geometric fact -- a plane has no privileged up. It is inherited from the reader's body and gravity. Either derive it from the reading situation or record it as a stated premise of the notation.

vertex-acts.statement: The Angle takes the initiating / source / writing role and the Curve the receiving / sink / reading one, in every domain the corpus uses. The pairing is domain-invariant; why the singular-curvature mark takes the source role is not derived.
vertex-acts.success_condition: CHANGED at F147, because the old one asked for three different things. Directedness IS derivable -- the Angle is rotation class 1, so its orientation is meaning-bearing (symmetry-order-is-operator-capacity) -- but the CURVE IS ALSO CLASS 1, so directedness cannot discriminate the pair. Agency and initiation are not geometric properties and no measurement returns them. And the second branch, 'find a different geometric property of the vertex', has been searched: 28 settled claims characterise the Angle's geometry and not one of those facts is semantic (F142 took the most tempting candidate and showed it to be a pun on `init`). What is missing is not another property but a MAP -- a principled reason why, of the two class-1 marks, the singular-curvature one takes the source role. That map would close a dozen claims at once, and it is the Tier-1-to-Tier-2 gap F48 named: the grammar is grounded, the vocabulary it composes is still largely chosen.
vertex-acts.scope: About the corpus, not about necessity. Establishes that the pairing is not arbitrary WITHIN this corpus -- it survives the domain axis -- and says nothing about why the geometry should carry it.

waveform-alphabet-is-exact.statement: Every drawn sign-mark decomposes into waveshape x phase x datum with no residue, and the corpus performs both of the operations that decomposition implies.
waveform-alphabet-is-exact.success_condition: Already measured. What would extend it is a reason the three waveshapes should be triangle, square and sine rather than any other three -- the completion result (curve-pair-is-the-circle) is the nearest thing and does not reach it.
waveform-alphabet-is-exact.scope: About the ALPHABET being generated by those three parameters, and about the corpus drawing the inversions and datum-additions out in full. Says nothing about whether the acoustic SEMANTICS are intended -- that is the domain question, and `the-domain-is-an-axis` answers it.

waveform-reading-is-intended.statement: WITHDRAWN. Asked whether the marks are to be read as waveforms, and required something that would establish the waveform reading as THE reading rather than one useful one.
waveform-reading-is-intended.why_withdrawn: The question is malformed, and the corpus says so in its own layout. `axis_census.json` has recorded since it was built that DOMAIN is an axis on three sheets -- PointShapeLineWaveAngleCurve (F10), VideoGamesProgrammingReactRedux (F18) and ZodiacSignSymbols (F39), with a fourth added at F139 -- and an axis is listed there only where a sheet VARIES it to distinguish cells. A notation that varies the domain deliberately, on three sheets, cannot have one. Worse for the original framing: the waveform features and the modality/element features are not rival readings of the marks but two names for ONE partition, since F46 settled that the geometry IS the modality. Asking which is the real reading asks which name for a partition is the real name. Retained under its own id so the 178 built pages and the tmpl.* strings that cite it reach the correction rather than a missing entry.

where-the-turning-gathers-is-an-axis-the.statement: Concentration says HOW MUCH of a run's turning gathers. WHERE it gathers is a separate quantity, it was fixed at the middle of the run without anyone noticing it was a parameter, and freeing it closes 37 per cent of the redraw gap.
where-the-turning-gathers-is-an-axis-the.success_condition: A figure whose turning gathers somewhere the grid can already put it.

z12-factors.statement: Z/12 = Z/3 x Z/4, so 3 modalities x 4 elements covers twelve cells with no repeat and no gap.
z12-factors.derivation: gcd(3,4)=1, Chinese Remainder Theorem. This is why there are twelve, not an observation that there happen to be.
